qt: to the Commission Seán Kelly (PPE) Subject:

Manufacturers increasingly tie vehicle components electronically to a single vehicle’s identification number (VIN), refusing to allow used parts to be coded to another vehicle, even by registered independent operators using the manufacturers’ own diagnostic systems. Regulation (EU) 2026/17381 encourages the reuse of parts, but this is undermined if software locks can block it. This raises costs for consumers, excludes independent garages, risks early write-offs and runs counter to circular economy goals. The practice is spreading to heavy goods vehicles (HGVs) and agricultural machinery. 1.
Has the Commission assessed the impact of VIN locking and part pairing on the reuse of safe used, refurbished and remanufactured parts?

Will it ensure that qualified independent operators, not only authorised treatment facilities, can access the tools to code and match parts on fair, non-discriminatory terms, without case-by-case manufacturer approval?
Will it ensure that such rights apply not only to cars, but also to HGVs, agricultural machinery and other equipment?
Regulation (EU) 2026/1738 of 8 July 2026 on circularity requirements for vehicle design and on management of end-of-life vehicles (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1738/oj). 1
